member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.CommandJournal
member.summary: The single mutation bus for a Project. Applies commands, tracks the dirty flag, and supports linear undo/redo. Doing a new command clears the redo stack — the standard model.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.CommandJournal.MarkDirty
member.summary: Flags unsaved changes for an edit made outside the command stack. Used by bulk operations such as propagating a type's wire encoding, which touch many bindings at once and are re-derivable from the type rather than individually undoable.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.CommandJournal.MarkSaved
member.summary: Called after a successful save. Clears dirty; keeps undo history intact.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.IEditCommand
member.summary: An undoable mutation of the model. Every edit made by the UI goes through the journal — that gives undo/redo, dirty tracking, an audit trail, and the operation stream Phase 6 collaboration ships.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.IEditCommand.Describe
member.summary: Human-readable label shown in the undo menu.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.RemoveModuleCommand
member.summary: Removes a module and every route that used it, restoring both on undo. Routes have to travel with the module: leaving them behind would point at a module that no longer exists.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.ChangeRouteCommand
member.summary: Swaps one leg for another in place, which is what changing a dropdown on an existing row means.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.Commands.ChangeEncodingCommand
member.summary: Replaces the encoding wholesale. The undo restores the previous instance — cheaper and simpler than tracking individual property changes, and encoding edits are already coarse-grained in the UI.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.IProjectRepository
member.summary: Read/write port for a project. WPF, CLI, and future backends (SQL in Phase 6) depend on this, not on any concrete storage. The JSON implementation lives in ProtoDesigner.Persistence.Json.

member.name: T:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator
member.summary: Pushes a type's wire representation onto every field binding that references it, anywhere in the project.
member.remarks:
The layout engine only ever reads on a binding, which is what keeps it language- and policy-free. But the product rule is that a type serialises the same way everywhere, so this is the one place that reconciles the two: edit the type, and every occurrence follows.
The scale is derived, never typed by hand: given a range and a width, the finest factor that still covers the range is (max - min) / (2^bits - 1), with the offset pinned to the range minimum.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator.ApplyAll(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.Project)
member.summary: Applies every type's wire settings across the whole project. Returns the number of bindings changed.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator.Apply(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.Project,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.TypeDefinition)
member.summary: Applies one type's wire settings to every binding that uses it.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator.Apply(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.TypeDefinition,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.FieldBinding)
member.summary: Writes the type's representation onto a single binding. Returns true if anything changed. Structs and arrays are skipped: their size is the sum of what they are built from, all the way down to primitives and enums, so they have no width of their own to set.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator.ResolveTransform(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.TypeDefinition,ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.IWireSized,System.Nullable{ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.NumericRange},System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: Works out the value-to-wire mapping for a type, honouring an explicit offset/scale when the user has set one and deriving the tightest fit otherwise.
member.remarks: The subtle case is a floating-point host sent as an integer. An integer wire code cannot carry a fractional value directly, so such a field needs a scale even at full width — a double in 8 wire bytes still has to map 64 bits of integer onto its declared range. Only a wire skips scaling, because there the IEEE bit pattern passes through untouched and scaling would corrupt it.

member.name: M:ProtoDesigner.Application.WireEncodingPropagator.AllBindings(ProtoDesigner.Core.Model.Project)
member.summary: Every binding in the project: message fields and struct members alike.
